# Functions
![](/images/function.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

R <u id='function_tooltip'>__Functions__</u> allow the user to carry out specific tasks. R has many inbuilt <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u> but you can also create your own. Currently we will look at inbuilt <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u>.

## Function layout

The basic layout of a <u id='function_tooltip'>__function__</u> is (don't type the below into `R`):

```{r eval=FALSE}
function_name(objects, options)
``` 

There are 3 main parts to the above:

- The __<u id='function_tooltip'>function</u> name__ (`function_name`)
- The __object/s__ to provide to the <u id='function_tooltip'>__function__</u>
    - This can be numbers, strings, <u id='variable_tooltip'>__variables__</u> we have created etc
    - Most <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u> require at least one __object__ 
    - Some <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u> can take multiple objects, if multiple __objects__ are provided they must be separated by `,`
- <u id='function_tooltip'>__Function__</u> options (`options`) 
    - Options can be provided to some <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u> to alter the way they will work
    - Some <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u> don't have options
    - Most options have default modes. If the options is not specified the default mode will be used
    - Like __objects__, when using multiple options they must be separated by `,`

## Numerical rounding examples

Try running the below commands in your Rstudio __console__ which utilise 4 different <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u>.

```{r eval=FALSE}
ceiling(3.5)
floor(3.5)
sqrt(9)
round(3.5555, digits = 2)
round(3.5555, digits = 3)
round(3.5555, digits = 0)
two <- sqrt(4)
``` 

## Help page

You may be able to intuit what the above <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u> do from their names and output.
However, if you are not sure/would like to be certain you can look at the help pages of <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u>.

The help page of <u id='function_tooltip'>__functions__</u> can be accessed in 2 main ways:

- Click on the __<u id='function_tooltip'>function</u> name__ so your cursor is in it and press __F1__.
- Type `?` followed by the __<u id='function_tooltip'>function</u> name__. Example below:

```{r eval=FALSE}
?ceiling
``` 

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Tippy tooltips
tippy::tippy_this(elementId = "operator_tooltip", 
                  tooltip = "+, -, /, *, etc.",
                  arrow = TRUE, placement = "bottom")
tippy::tippy_this(elementId = "variable_tooltip", 
                  tooltip = "Container of an R object with a name",
                  arrow = TRUE, placement = "bottom")
tippy::tippy_this(elementId = "function_tooltip", 
                  tooltip = "Named block of code that performs a specific task",
                  arrow = TRUE, placement = "bottom")
```
